title: Model Fallback Economics & Enterprise Procurement Survey
creator: Avery Chen
description: Goal: quantify how enterprise customers trade latency, cost, and accuracy when Redwood falls back to alternative model variants (quantized, smaller/flavors, regional mirrors). Produce direct recommendations for routing policies, pricing thresholds, and procurement guardrails aimed at Dedicated and Private customers. Deliverables: 1) competitive analysis of how providers surface fallback options and pricing for enterprise SLAs, 2) a short procurement-focused survey and interview plan to capture buyer preferences, 3) a simulation workbook that projects customer-level unit economics for fallback decisions, and 4) recommended Console UX signals and runtime policies to make fallbacks observable and controllable by customers.
acceptance_criteria: Competitive landscape memo with at least 8 vendor examples and a 1-page comparison table
Survey instrument (10–12 questions) validated by Sales and Legal and run against 50+ enterprise contacts
Simulation workbook with scenario-sensitive cost/latency/quality curves and at least 3 customer archetypes
Clear set of product recommendations (routing policy defaults, UI controls, telemetry events) and a migration plan for Dedicated customers
PM + Eng + SRE sign-off on proposed runtime telemetry events and a GH issue for implementation
tasks: Draft vendor analysis template and populate initial vendor rows
Design survey and interview script; schedule 12 buyer interviews with AMs
Build simulation model in spreadsheet (token-level cost, fallback frequency, latency delta, quality penalty)
Align with SRE/Serving runtime on telemetry payloads and fallback reason codes
Create Console UI mockups showing fallback exposure and opt controls
Prepare a one-page recommendation for sales/solutions engineering to use in renewals
